name: Scrap aluminium
description: A handful of aluminium offcuts: torn sheet, a bent strip of angle and a sawn ring of tube. Light, and useful for repairs.
notes: Two torn sheet pieces, a bent angle strip and a 15 mm ring of tube scattered on about 90 by 60 mm. CHECK VOLUME (x4.4): the box counts the air between loose pieces; the metal itself is about 19 ml against the reference's 20 ml. alu-bare draws every piece.

name: Brass chunks
description: A few heavy pieces of scrap brass: a stub of hex bar, a short threaded pipe fitting and a flattened lump.
notes: A 25 mm hex bar stub, a threaded pipe nipple and a folded lump on about 90 by 70 mm, drawn in brass.

name: Scrap cast iron
description: A few broken shards of cast iron, the biggest a curved piece of a pan rim. Brittle, but it can be melted down.
notes: A thick curved rim piece and three small shards on about 60 by 50 mm, drawn in iron-cast. CHECK VOLUME (x4.1): the box counts the air between loose shards; the iron is about 7 ml against the reference's 8 ml.

name: Copper chunk
description: A sheared-off length of thick copper bar, bent at one end. Good for wiring and repairs once worked.
notes: A 25 by 10 mm bus bar about 75 mm long with a slanted shear at one end and a bend at the other, drawn in copper.

name: Scrap tin
description: Strips and torn pieces of thin tin plate cut from cans, one curled up and one still ribbed.
notes: Flat torn sheet, a ribbed can-wall panel, a curled piece and a strip on about 80 by 50 mm. CHECK VOLUME (x10.4): the sheet is 0.6 mm thick (thicker than real tin plate so it survives the 2 mm grain) and the box counts the air round a curl and loose strips. No tin finish exists; steel-bright stands in for the bright tin plate.

name: Steel spike
description: A crudely forged, rusty steel spike on a square plate with two bolt holes, made to be bolted onto something. Awkward to swing.
notes: A 280 mm spike, 30 mm square at the root, drawn as square sections that narrow and step up where the point bends, on a 60 mm plate with two painted bolt holes. CHECK VOLUME (x4.0): the reference's 250 ml is a bulk volume; the steel itself is about 70 ml, and the box counts the air round a taper. The reference's quality is a butchering penalty, so the draft brings no quality. Mounting on a vehicle has no field yet. Held by the shank.

name: Split stone helmet
description: A huge cone-shaped helmet of dense black stone, cracked clean in two. Bundles of fine bright metal tubes jut from the break.
notes: Two half-cones 700 mm across and 500 mm tall lying 140 mm apart, grey on the broken faces, with five metal tubes standing out of each face; the halves are stepped stacks, since compound pieces cannot taper a half-cone. The size matches the 150 kg mass for dense stone. CHECK VOLUME (x73): the reference's 4 L cannot hold 150 kg of anything; the stone is about 64 L. obsidian draws the stone, stone-grey the break and mithril the tubes. Too heavy to carry; the size is a placeholder. Name and description avoid the source's lore; whether Deadvox wants this salvage is a content call.

name: Giant stinger
description: A barbed stinger as long as a hand, cut from a giant insect with its venom sac still attached. Too light to make a good weapon.
notes: A 130 mm barbed shaft in chitin-black with a chitin-brown root and a lumpy, flattened sac in flesh-membrane on a short neck, 180 mm overall. Held by the shaft. Infected usage stands in for harvest from mutant insects until a harvest source exists.
